text: Rapid population ageing, urban migration, and the weakening of multigenerational households have left many older adults in Chinese cities facing intertwined physical decline, psychological distress, social loss, and a diminished sense of purpose. Conventional responses tend to be specialized and clinical and are often experienced by older Chinese adults as fragmented, unfamiliar, or stigmatizing. Collective ritual, defined as structured group practices using culturally familiar forms, such as greeting, blessing, mutual recognition, coordinated movement, communal singing, embrace, sharing, and role-taking to cultivate connection, emotion regulation, and meaning, is an ancient and culturally embedded practice that has always addressed body, mind, emotion, relationship, and spirit together.
source_label: A ritual way of ageing well: a qualitative study of a comprehensive, culturally grounded ritual-based health programme for older adults in urban China
